title: Stop Guessing: Build Robust AI with Layered CoT
talk_summary: A conceptual overview of multi-agent systems and chain-of-thought prompting, proposing 'layered CoT' where each generated reasoning step is verified against a knowledge base or ensemble before the next step proceeds.

takeaways.technique: Per-step verification gate instead of end-only review
takeaways.what_they_do: After each reasoning step, the output is cross-checked against a structured knowledge base, fact-checker, or second model before the next step is allowed to build on it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Before moving on, the generated thought is immediately verified... cross-referencing the output against a structured knowledge base or an external database.

takeaways.technique: Verifier agent as a distinct role in the pipeline
takeaways.what_they_do: Treats verification as its own specialized agent/step that checks each produced artifact, rather than folding checking into the producer.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a model ensemble model to check for the accuracy. But this verification step is really crucial.

takeaways.technique: Explicit step-by-step reasoning with auditable steps
takeaways.what_they_do: Prompts ask the model to enumerate reasoning steps so mistakes are visible and debuggable at each stage.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If we spot a mistake in any of the intermediate step, we can adjust the prompt or the process

takeaways.what_they_do: Notes that near-identical prompts yield different CoT outputs, and argues per-step verification reduces this sensitivity.
takeaways.evidence_quote: two almost identical prompts might yield vastly different chain of thought, complicating both reproducibility and reliability.
